title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is in the 'Longue Marche' continuation, in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type framework. M[Γ_0] is a group (or monoid) of automorphisms u of a profinite 'lego' fundamental-group configuration. Each u is attached to an element α ∈ Π̂_{02}, normalized and defined by u(ρ) = int(α)ρ. χ(u) is a character with sign components ε_2(u), ε_3(u) ∈ {±1}, and τ' is an involution. On the previous page Grothendieck showed that α'' (attached to u'' = u'u) satisfies α'' = ε α' α. He also showed that this naive normalization is not multiplicative.

On this page he changes variables. Put a = ε_3(τ') α^{-1} u, where ε_3(τ') = 1 if ε_3 = 1 and ε_3(τ') = τ' if ε_3 = −1. Do the same for a' and a''. Since ε''_3 = ε_3 ε'_3, the composition law becomes a'' = ε a' a (62). The sign is given by (63): ε = +1 iff ε_3 = 1 or ε'_2 ε'_3 = 1, and ε = −1 iff ε_3 = −1 and ε'_2 ε'_3 = −1.

He then tests whether the expected crossed-homomorphism (1-cocycle) law α'' = ε u'(α) α' (64) holds. Here u'(α) = u' α u'^{-1} is computed in the ambient semidirect product.
- Inverting (61) gives α = u a^{-1} ε_3(τ').
- Hence α'' = ε u'u a^{-1} a'^{-1} ε'_3(τ') ε_3(τ').
- By contrast, ε u'(α) α' = ε u'u a^{-1} ε_3(τ') a'^{-1} ε'_3(τ').
- So (64) is equivalent to [ε_3(τ'), a'^{-1}] = 1, which is automatic when ε_3 = 1.
- When ε_3 = −1 it is a 'draconian restriction' on a', and false in general.

The always-valid formula is α'' = (ε u'(α) α') · ε'_3(τ')([a', ε_3(τ')]), with the commutator conjugated by ε'_3(τ'). It can also be written [ε'_3(τ')(a'), ε_3(τ')]. In other words, the assignment u ↦ α is a 1-cocycle only up to a sign and a commutator correction.

Purpose. The next page calls this 'le monstre' (formula 65). He then asks whether the central extension of Z^!_{ρ,σ} ≅ U^![σ] by μ = {±1} is trivial, knowing that its restrictions to two subgroups split. The computation serves the determination of a sign extension in his Teichmüller/GT-type automorphism groups.
errors: No substantive error. Check: write x = a'^{-1}, e = ε_3(τ'), f = ε'_3(τ'). Then (ε u'(α)α')^{-1} α'' = f^{-1} x^{-1} e^{-1} x f e. Since e, f commute and are involutions, this equals f[a', e]f = ε'_3(τ')([a', ε_3(τ')]), as written. The underbraced form [ε'_3(τ')(a'), ε_3(τ')] is also correct.

Minor imprecision: 'au vu de (*)' reduces (64) to [ε_3(τ'), a'^{-1}] = 1. Strictly the condition is x f e = e x f, which is equivalent because e and f commute. So the statement is right, but one step is suppressed.
The derivation implicitly uses τ'^2 = 1 and the centrality of the sign ε in the ambient group, both needed for ε''_3(τ') = ε'_3(τ') ε_3(τ').

ideas.what: Renormalizing the elements α attached to automorphisms u (via a = ε_3(τ') α^{-1} u, with an involution inserted according to a sign character) so that composition becomes a'' = ε a' a with an explicit sign rule.
ideas.modern_name: composition law / multiplication in a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group, sign-twisted
ideas.usually_credited_to: GT composition law: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; the sign-twisted variant with characters ε_2, ε_3 is not standard in the literature

ideas.what: Showing that α'' = ε u'(α)α' (cocycle condition) fails when ε_3 = −1, and computing the exact commutator correction term.
ideas.modern_name: failure of a crossed homomorphism / non-abelian 1-cocycle up to a correction term

ideas.what: Reducing the whole question to the triviality of a central extension by μ_2 of Z^!_{ρ,σ}, given splittings on two subgroups (next page).
ideas.modern_name: central extension by Z/2 / sign obstruction class in H^2

missed.claim: Grothendieck develops an explicit sign-twisted composition law for the elements attached to (possibly orientation-reversing, ε_3 = −1) automorphisms in his Teichmüller-tower/GT-type groups. The non-cocycle correction is an explicit commutator with an involution. This is a hand computation feeding the question of whether a μ_2 central extension splits, and its resolution lies on later pages.
missed.quote: La formule toujours correcte est α''=(ε u'(α)α').ε'_3(τ')([a',ε_3(τ')])
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Extended GT groups that include sign/orientation characters (e.g. versions incorporating complex conjugation) are studied today. An explicit cocycle-correction formula could be compared with those, but this page alone is a routine verification.

deep.surprise_reason: A correct but technical group-theoretic computation, a 'monstre' sign/commutator correction to a cocycle law in Grothendieck's GT-type setting. It is interesting as working detail but is not a new idea or connection in itself.
transcription_corrections: Top '601' is Grothendieck's own pagination; the archive page is 594.
In (63) the condition reads 'ε'_2 ε'_3 = 1' (the subscript 2 is overwritten in the image); first line: 'ε_3 = 1 ou ε'_2ε'_3 = 1'.

Left margin (rotated) seems to read something like 'par erreur j'écrivais' rather than 'par raison de symétrie'. Together with the struck words it means he had mistakenly believed one could have (64).
On the next page, '(61) gives ε'_3(τ')a' = α'^{-1}u'' should read a', not α', which is consistent with (61).
